findings.title: ZIP import writes members outside the import folder
findings.attacker: Any signed-in user; controls the uploaded archive, not the server's filesystem or configuration.
findings.source: Member names inside an uploaded ZIP archive.
findings.control: The containment check compares the joined path as a string prefix before normalizing it, so '../' segments pass.
findings.sink: Writing each member's bytes to the joined destination path.
findings.path: POST /import (routes.py) passes the upload to extract_zip, which joins each member name to the import folder, checks the prefix, then writes the file.
findings.impact: Overwrite files the service account can write outside the import folder, including configuration read at startup.
exposure_assumptions: The import route is enabled (it is by default in config/defaults.py).
findings.counterevidence: Searched for later normalization or a sandboxed write helper between the check and the write; none found. The service account's write access outside the data folder is not established from source.
proof_gaps: Whether the deployed service account can write outside the data folder.
findings.investigation_question: Upload a ZIP with a member named '../outside.txt' to /import in an isolated copy: the expected safe behaviour is rejection; the finding holds if outside.txt is written beside the import folder.

confidence.reason: The prefix check before normalization and the reachable write are both visible in source.

findings.title: TAR import follows member names and links outside the import folder
findings.attacker: Any signed-in user; controls the uploaded archive.
findings.source: Member names and link targets inside an uploaded TAR archive.
findings.control: extract_tar calls the library's extract-all with no member filter, so absolute names, '../' names, and symbolic links are honoured.
findings.sink: Extracting all members into the import folder.
findings.path: POST /import with a .tar upload reaches extract_tar, which extracts every member without filtering.
findings.impact: Write or link files outside the import folder, as for the ZIP path.
exposure_assumptions: The Python version in use does not apply a safe default extraction filter.
findings.counterevidence: Searched for a filter argument or a pre-extraction member check; none found. Newer Python versions apply a default filter, which would block most of this.
proof_gaps: The Python version used in deployment.
findings.investigation_question: Upload a TAR with a '../outside.txt' member and a symbolic link to /tmp in an isolated copy on the deployed Python version: the finding holds if either is created outside the import folder.

confidence.reason: Reachability is shown in source, but the effect depends on the deployed Python version's default extraction filter, which the repository does not pin.

findings.title: Login handler redirects to any URL in the next parameter
findings.attacker: An unauthenticated attacker who can send a victim a link.
findings.source: The next query parameter of GET /login.
findings.control: None: the handler passes next to the redirect without checking its host.
findings.path: GET /login?next=... stores next and redirects to it after successful sign-in.
findings.impact: Send a signed-in victim to an attacker-controlled site that appears to come from the application, aiding phishing.
findings.counterevidence: Searched for a host allowlist or relative-URL check in the handler and in the response middleware; none found.
findings.investigation_question: Sign in through /login?next=https://example.test in an isolated copy: the expected safe behaviour is a redirect within the application; the finding holds if the browser is sent to example.test.

confidence.reason: Direct in source; impact depends on how the login page is used.

findings.title: Debug route returns environment variable names and values
findings.attacker: Anyone who can reach the service when debug mode is on.
findings.control: The route is registered only when DEBUG is set; there is no authentication on it.
findings.sink: Serializing the process environment into the response.
findings.path: GET /debug/env returns the environment when the debug flag enables the route.
findings.impact: Disclose secrets held in environment variables, such as the database password variable.
exposure_assumptions: DEBUG is enabled in the deployment, which the stage 1 model does not establish.
findings.counterevidence: DEBUG defaults to off in config/defaults.py; no deployment file in the repository turns it on.
findings.investigation_question: With DEBUG enabled in an isolated copy, request /debug/env without signing in: the finding holds if environment values are returned.

confidence.reason: Depends on a deployment choice the repository does not show.
